tests.notes: CORRECTED: the error only triggers when an uninitialized local storage pointer is actually USED (read/written), not merely declared -- a declared-but-unused one only gets an 'unused local variable' warning
internal functions can return storage pointers since internal calls never cross the ABI boundary
public/external functions cannot return storage pointers -- no ABI representation for a raw storage reference
compile-level check only -- does not verify at runtime that both references genuinely alias the same mutation
CORRECTED: delete works on a member access reached through a storage reference (ref.value), not on the reference variable itself -- see 010 for the disallowed direct form
delete cannot be applied directly to a storage pointer variable -- ambiguous whether it should delete the underlying data or unset the pointer
